prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same bug in `pre_parse_json` (src/mcp/server/mcpserver/utilities/func_metadata.py): when a tool parameter's annotation is a union that includes `str` (e.g. `str | None`), the code unconditionally tries `json.loads()` on incoming string values, corrupting legitimate strings that happen to look like JSON (e.g. "null", "123", "[foo]"). Both PRs modify the exact same guard clause (`isinstance(data_value, str) and field_info.annotation is not str`) to add a smarter check before pre-parsing. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same bug in `pre_parse_json` (src/mcp/server/mcpserver/utilities/func_metadata.py): when a tool parameter's annotation is a union that includes `str` (e.g. `str | None`), the code unconditionally tries `json.loads()` on incoming string values, corrupting legitimate strings that happen to look like JSON (e.g. "null", "123", "[foo]"). Both PRs modify the exact same guard clause (`isinstance(data_value, str) and field_info.annotation is not str`) to add a smarter check before pre-parsing. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated()` and explicitly strips `Annotated[...]` off each union member before checking for `str | None`, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the idiomatic FastMCP pattern `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` (very common for documented optional string params). #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json()` instead checks union args against a `frozenset({str, int, float, bool, type(None)})` via `in`, which does not match an `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` member (it isn't equal to plain `str`), so `_should_pre_parse_json` still returns True and the corruption bug persists for that common annotated-optional-string case. #2032 does cover a broader set of pure-primitive unions (e.g. `str | int`, `str | bool`) that #3056 doesn't handle, so that gap should be filed as a follow-up on top of #3056 rather than reverting to #2032's approach.

clusters.pick_reason: #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated()` and explicitly strips `Annotated[...]` off each union member before checking for `str | None`, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the idiomatic FastMCP pattern `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` (very common for documented optional string params). #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json()` instead checks union args against a `frozenset({str, int, float, bool, type(None)})` via `in`, which does not match an `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` member (it isn't equal to plain `str`), so `_should_pre_parse_json` still returns True and the corruption bug persists for that common annotated-optional-string case. #2032 does cover a broader set of pure-primitive unions (e.g. `str | int`, `str | bool`) that #3056 doesn't handle, so that gap should be filed as a follow-up on top of #3056 rather than reverting to #2032's approach.

clusters.pick_reason: #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated()` and explicitly strips `Annotated[...]` off each union member before checking for `str | None`, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the idiomatic FastMCP pattern `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` (very common for documented optional string params). #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json()` instead checks union args against a `frozenset({str, int, float, bool, type(None)})` via `in`, which does not match an `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` member (it isn't equal to plain `str`), so `_should_pre_parse_json` still returns True and the corruption bug persists for that common annotated-optional-string case. #2032 does cover a broader set of pure-primitive unions (e.g. `str | int`, `str | bool`) that #3056 doesn't handle, so that gap should be filed as a follow-up on top of #3056 rather than reverting to #2032's approach.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #3041 splits the whole header into top-level challenge segments first (_split_www_authenticate_segments) and then explicitly locates the Bearer scheme segment via _extract_bearer_auth_params, so it correctly handles headers with multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=..., Bearer error=...'). PR #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only splits on the first space in the whole header and treats everything after as one param list, which conflates scheme boundaries when multiple auth schemes are present in a single header.
